title: Generic generators lifted into a finite local subsystem
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], Lambda a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and phi:F to G a monomorphism of Lambda-module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Assume G is finite locally constant [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant]. For a component generic point eta [def-sc-generic-point], there exist an open U containing eta, an irreducible scheme Y, a surjective etale map f:Y to U, and a generic point xi of Y mapping to eta. There exist a finite locally constant module sheaf H on Y and a monomorphism psi:H to (f followed by U into X)^*F which is an epimorphism on every geometric stalk over xi [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. This asserts only generic generation, not that psi is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09BH, Proposition 59.74.1 (3), generic-neighbourhood argument before Noetherian induction; etale-cohomology.tex, proposition-constructible-over-noetherian

proof.text: Remove all irreducible components other than the component with generic point eta. Choose an etale trivialization of G above eta, and isolate the component through that generic point. Its open neighbourhood is irreducible, and the constant value M of G is finitely generated because it is a geometric stalk.

Exactness identifies the generic stalk N of F with a submodule of M. Noetherianity of the coefficient ring makes N finitely generated. Lift a finite set of generators to sections on one common pointed etale neighbourhood. Refine until their images equal the corresponding constant sections, using the filtered-colimit description of the stalk.

Linear relations among the lifted sections vanish because their images vanish in constant M and F maps monically to constant M. Thus the lifts induce a monomorphism from the constant sheaf N to F on the neighbourhood. Isolate the component through the chosen generic point again, calling the resulting irreducible neighbourhood Y and its generic point xi. H is this constant N sheaf, so it is finite locally constant and its map to F is epi at the chosen geometric point over xi. Stalks at any two separably closed extensions of the residue field are identified using compatible separable closures; these identifications commute with the inclusion into constant M. Thus epimorphy holds at every geometric point over xi. Its monicity follows from monicity of the constant inclusion N into M, checked on stalks. If N is zero use the zero constant sheaf.

Take U to be the open image of Y in X. Etale morphisms are open, so U contains eta, and the induced map f:Y to U is etale and surjective. The generic point xi maps to eta, since the neighbourhood was pointed at a geometric point over eta. No equality between H and F away from xi, nor descent of H to U, is used.

theorem exists_generic_generating_locallyConstant_subsheaf
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] {Λ : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    {F G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)}
    (φ : F ⟶ G) [Mono φ] [IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf G]
    (η : X) (hη : η ∈ genericPoints X) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_hU : η ∈ U) (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ U.toScheme),
      Etale f ∧ Surjective f ∧ IrreducibleSpace Y ∧
      ∃ (ξ : Y), IsGenericPoint ξ Set.univ ∧ U.ι (f ξ) = η ∧
      ∃ (H : Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
        (ψ : H ⟶ (Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (f ≫ U.ι)).obj F),
        Mono ψ ∧ IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf H ∧
        ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y),
          s (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω) = ξ →
          Epi ((pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber.map ψ)
